archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A stationary, well-protected thrower in a run-first Stefanski offense whose value comes from pushing the ball 10+ yards downfield rather than from accuracy or his legs.

report.headline: Clean pocket, live deep ball, but the middle of the field keeps biting
report.take:
Penix took over in Week 3 after Cooper Rush and Tua Tagovailoa started the first two games, and the profile is consistent with his first two seasons. He is a downfield passer working behind the best-protected pocket in the league. Atlanta's offHitRate ranks 1st of 32, and he is pressured on just 12% of dropbacks, 4th of 42. That keeps his sack rate at 4.3%, 10th of 49. The offense is built around the run: passRateOverExp is -6.5, 28th of 32, and the rushing EPA ranks 5th. So volume is modest at 28.4 attempts a game, and his value has to come from efficiency on the throws he does get.

That efficiency is split almost exactly at the 10-yard line. On throws of 10+ air yards he is at +0.365 EPA per attempt, and the 19 deep shots are at +0.797. Under 10 yards the group sits at -0.071. Most of that comes from 43 throws behind the line, which cost 19.5 EPA. That is largely screens and swing passes, and Bijan Robinson's -0.24 EPA per target says the design is failing as much as the quarterback. The real flaw is accuracy. His CPOE of -4.26 ranks 39th, and he ran -4.4 and -3.6 the two prior years, so this is who he is rather than a slump. The one genuine improvement is his bad-throw rate, down to 14.6% from 22.5% last year, with a quicker 2.62-second release.

The topline hides two things. First, his season EPA per dropback of 0.005 is propped up by 20 plays with a 9+ point lead, which were worth +1.085 apiece. In one-score games he is at -0.107, and trailing by 9+ he is at -0.109. Second, the interceptions have a clear address: four of his six came over the middle, where his EPA is -0.348. Throwing left he has none on 93 attempts.

The arc is down after a hot start. Weeks 3-4 were his two cleanest games, both wins. The last five weeks went 1-4 with -0.118 EPA per dropback. The Week 8 shutout at Tampa (8/24, four picks, -24.1 EPA) against the league's No. 2 defense drags the last-three numbers hardest. But Week 9 against a middling Cincinnati defense was also negative, so it isn't only one bad afternoon.

strengths.title: The downfield throws pay
strengths.body: His completion rate on 20+ yard throws is low, which is normal for that depth, but the throws he connects on swing drives. That makes the 10+ air-yard game where nearly all his positive EPA lives. Last year's aggressiveness was almost identical, so the willingness to throw into tight windows downfield is stable. The deep EPA itself rests on 19 attempts and will cool somewhat, but the intermediate-plus game is a real skill.

strengths.title: A clean pocket, few sacks
strengths.body: He is rarely touched, and the low sack rate comes mainly from the protection. When pressure does arrive, it turns into sacks at a high rate: his pressure-to-sack rate ranks 32nd of 42. He is not a play-extender, scrambling on 3.7% of dropbacks. As long as the line holds up, that weakness rarely shows, and that protection has been consistent all year.

strengths.title: Red zone and the London connection
strengths.body: Inside the 20 he has 8 touchdowns and no interceptions despite a 48.6% completion rate. Near the goal line he takes his shot to a spot and lives with incompletions rather than forcing throws. Drake London is the engine, at +0.515 EPA on 57 targets, far above anyone else. A red-zone TD rate on 37 plays will drift, but the London volume is a durable floor.

concerns.title: Turnovers over the middle
concerns.body: His interception rate of 3% ranks 37th of 49, up from 0.33 picks a game last year to 0.86 now. Four of the six came over the middle, where his completion rate drops to 54.5% and CPOE to -12.6. The last three games hit a 5.6% pick rate, inflated by the four-interception day in Tampa. The middle-of-field problem is too concentrated to wave off as noise, but some regression toward his career rate is likely.

concerns.title: Accuracy is a career trait
concerns.body: CPOE has been negative in all three seasons, and at -4.26 it is nearly the same as his rookie mark. Some of this season's figure comes from failed screens behind the line (-15.8 CPOE there), which is partly scheme. Still, 44.4% completion on intermediate throws is on him. Don't expect this to change mid-season.

concerns.title: Front-running inflates the line
concerns.body: Twenty snaps with a 9+ point lead produced +1.085 EPA each with an 80% completion rate. Everywhere else he has been below average. In one-score games, where the outcome is decided, he sits at -0.107. The overall 0.005 overstates how he plays when the game is in doubt.

trend.note: Two efficient wins in Weeks 3-4 gave way to a jagged 1-4 stretch: good games against Baltimore and San Francisco, bad ones against Chicago, Tampa and Cincinnati. The last three games average -0.189 EPA per dropback, with the Tampa shutout doing most of the damage.

nextGame.headline: Kansas City's thin secondary invites shots, but short throws die
nextGame.body:
Kansas City's defense is strong in the place where Penix is weakest and soft in the place where he is strongest. The Chiefs are 4th in short-pass EPA allowed, so the screen-and-checkdown game that already bleeds EPA should struggle again. They rank 21st against deep passes and generate almost no pressure, ranking 27th in hit rate and 31st in sack rate. That matters for a passer whose pressured dropbacks turn into sacks so often. KC has been stingy to quarterbacks overall, 2nd in TDs allowed to the position, and its run defense ranks 5th. That could push a run-first Atlanta into more dropbacks than usual.

Availability tilts toward the shot plays. Mansoor Delane (79% of snaps) is out and L'Jarius Sneed is on IR, so the Chiefs are down two corners against a team whose WR1 production is London's. On the other side, Patrick Mahomes is questionable with an elbow strain, and tackle Jaylon Moore and receiver Xavier Worthy are day-to-day. A full-strength Mahomes and a top-4 offense would push Atlanta into catch-up mode, where Penix has been below average. A limited Mahomes keeps the game in Bijan Robinson's hands. Brian Robinson Jr.'s move to IR thins Atlanta's backfield behind Bijan but doesn't change much for Penix.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots versus depleted corners
keyMatchups.body: KC's deep-pass EPA allowed of 0.504 ranks 21st, and two corners who played most of the snaps are out or on IR. Penix's best throws are the 20+ yarders. If Atlanta calls even a handful of them in a clean pocket, this is where his EPA comes from.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a wall
keyMatchups.body: The Chiefs allow -0.115 EPA on short passes, 4th best. Penix's throws behind the line have already cost 19.5 EPA. Expect another drag from the screen game unless the play-calling shifts away from it.

keyMatchups.title: Pitts over London
keyMatchups.body: KC has held WR1s to -0.1 EPA per target, 2nd stingiest, but lets tight ends run over their averages (25th). Tight ends also draw an above-league share of targets against them. Kyle Pitts at +0.296 per target is the logical outlet if London is blanketed.

nextGame.watch: Whether he keeps the ball out of the middle of the field. With little pass rush coming, the danger is a forced throw over the middle, not a sack.

restOfSeason.body:
The sustainable parts are the protection, the London-heavy target tree, and a downfield game that will produce explosive plays at low volume. The run-first identity caps him around 28-30 attempts and roughly 190-225 yards most weeks. The accuracy is not going to change, and the 'leading by 9+' garbage-time padding will be harder to come by on a team now under .500. His EPA should settle near league average, not climb back to early-season levels.

Expect interceptions to regress somewhat toward his career norm but stay above last year's rate, because the middle-of-field mistakes are a pattern. Touchdowns should hold near the current pace on the strength of his red-zone work, though perfect ball security inside the 20 won't last forever. He is a steady 13-15 point fantasy option with a low floor against good defenses, as Tampa showed.
swingFactors: Ball security over the middle of the field
Atlanta's pass rate if games turn into shootouts
Health of the offensive line that keeps him clean

confidence.note: Seven starts and 199 attempts; accuracy and protection match his career, but the deep split and INT spike rest on small samples.
